get.description:
The ready-made studies the Studio’s New run page offers, word for word.

Each template states the question it answers, its setup, what it shows and what it cannot show, in the words the Studio prints, and carries what it launches: run is the environment (the scenario id, the season length, the house bots under env.anchors), trials and seed_mode the series, and on an experiment arms (a list of arms with the frame or seat settings each one sets, or per_seat for one arm per roster seat), metric and secondary_metrics. To launch one, send run with your own roster to the runs endpoint, with trials for a series, or build the experiment body from its arms; min_seats is the roster the arms need. A template names no model. experiment_size is the line every experiment template prints under its setup. Free tokens may call this.

post.description:
What a launch of this body would cost and commit, or the refusal it would get. Nothing is queued.

The same validation and receipts as a launch: plan ceilings, who funds each seat, the agent-turn reservation, the USD and wall-clock range, quota and queue headroom, and how much precision the trial count buys. funding has one entry per roster seat, in order: user (billed to your keys), sponsored (the platform pays, where offered) or guest (an invited seat, played on the guest’s own keys and left out of the reservation and the cost range). A body a launch would refuse answers with the launch’s error code. Free tokens may call this.

The top-level cost fields (usdLow, usdHigh, agentTurns, minutesLow, minutesHigh) are ONE trial; batch is the same figures for every trial you asked for, which is what the launch actually commits. hitsRunCap says the plan’s run-time cap is what ended the wall-clock range, not the scenario.

perSeat[].source says where each seat’s price came from: catalog is the provider’s own published rate, table a tier in Daishi’s price table, and fallback a pattern standing in for a model nobody has priced yet. approximate is true when any seat is fallback, and it means the whole band is a guess — the spend cap is still enforced against it, so a model priced above its vendor’s cheapest tier can pass a cap it would really have crossed.

get.description:
The meter’s record of your runs and where the account stands against the plan this month.

The same view the Studio’s Usage page reads. allowances carries the counters the run manager enforces with: agent turns used, held by queued runs and remaining (limit and remaining are null on a plan with no monthly cap), runs at once (queued_runs), the per-run spend cap, the access tokens and connected apps held against the plan’s allowance, and the per-minute ceiling. months, models and runs roll the meter up by UTC month, by model and per run, with spend split by who paid (your own key or the operator’s sponsorship). Invited seats on a peer’s own keys are counted as guest_seats and never metered.

200.description: The meter’s record of your runs and where the account stands against the plan this month.

get.description:
Every finished run rolled up by model: the figures the Studio’s Models page draws.

The same view the Studio’s Models page reads. models has a row per model over every finished run the account has (a run picked up by a new release mid-match, and any run not finished, stay out): runs and seats, mean, median, best and worst Fitness Index, fitness_ci (a Student t interval over distinct worlds, null below two), wins (the top Index in a run), survival with its Wilson interval, and provisional below the ranking floor. head_to_head counts, for each pair of models that shared a run, which one’s best seat scored higher. points is every seat as the chart draws it, with its run, world and dimension scores. pooled says how many runs, experiments, series and standalone runs the figures mix: an experiment’s arms differ on purpose, so a mean over them mixes the conditions its design kept apart. rubric and caveat are the comparability rule: scores compare within one scenario id and hash and one rubric.

The paired report as scored right now: per arm, per pair, each comparison against the control, the decision and a verdict.

The same report the Studio’s experiment panel shows. experiment.arms lists each arm with what it changes against the control (differs_from_control, paths of the arm’s request), its trial counts, its score over the scored trials (mean, interquartile mean, median, spread, a 95% Student t interval over the arm’s trials), cost, usage (spend per finished trial, spend per index point, and per model the tokens and spend per seat per trial over its scored trials, in that model’s own tokens; guest seats are counted as unmeasured_seats and enter no figure), and the awareness split (how many seats said they were being evaluated and how they scored against the seats that said the match was real). An experiment that declares output per turn, as its metric or a secondary outcome, gives each arm effort: per model the mean output tokens per play turn over its measured seats, thinking tokens per turn alone (null when the route itemized none), the share of play turns cut off at the seat’s output cap, and which upstream hosts served its calls, with how many seats were measured, how many missed more than a tenth of their rounds (short_seats) and how many had nothing to read (unmeasured_seats: a guest, or no output reported); each figure is in that model’s own tokens and compares only with the same model. Output per turn analyzes on the log scale: an arm’s per-trial value is the geometric mean over the seats measured in every arm that trial, so a difference is the mean of each model’s log ratio against itself, and its detail prints it as a percent change. experiment.pairs is every trial index with the per-arm value and its seeds; a trial index is excluded and says why when any arm’s trial there failed, was cancelled, lost a seat to an error, was stopped short of its season by the spend cap, was picked up by a new server release mid-match (its resumes: from that round its seats played without their memory of the earlier rounds, a condition the other arm did not play) or has not finished, because a half-played match never enters a pair; an arm whose comparison already stopped is not needed after its last pair, and the control only while some comparison still is, so a trial missing there excludes nothing. experiment.comparisons is each arm against the control: paired trials seen (n) and the last trial index among them (last_trial), the mean difference on the analysis scale, the rule’s stop, reason and verdict (arm_better, control_better, undecided, or null when the rule has not looked or had fewer than 3 pairs to look at; output per turn and the debrief share, which have no better side, read arm_higher or control_higher) with its interval, and a comparison that stopped keeps the numbers of its stop; a finished experiment the rule never stopped (a trial failed or could not be scored, so fewer pairs than trials) gets the rule’s last look on the pairs present, and its detail says how many trial indexes produced no pair. exact is the fixed rule’s exact two-sided sign-flip test at its look, beside the t test the rule reads: unit pair, or world when worlds repeat (each world’s pairs flip together), how many units, the p, and min_p, the smallest p so few units allow whatever the effect (0.0625 at five, which no exact test can bring under 0.05). It decides nothing, and is null under the anytime rule (which looks again and again, so a test read at its stop holds no level), before the look, and past 20 units. by_world is null when every pair played a world of its own; when the pairs replayed worlds (a seed pool of fewer maps than trials, or one pinned map) it gives how many world seeds the pairs played (worlds), how many more than once (repeated), and the cluster-robust Student t interval that counts each world once (CR1, on worlds minus one degrees of freedom, at the comparison’s level), which is what carries to worlds drawn the same way: the rule’s own interval counts pairs and holds for the worlds played. That interval is null under the anytime rule, below three worlds, and when the worlds came out alike. reason is owner for a comparison the owner stopped (the experiment cancelled, or its arm dropped in the Studio): under the anytime rule past its first look it keeps the sequence’s interval and verdict at that stop, which holds at any stopping time; under the fixed rule, or before the first look, its verdict is null, since a single look read early at a time the owner chose holds no level. The verdict sentence names how many trials each arm lost when the losses fall unevenly. experiment.secondary is each outcome declared beside the metric, in the order declared: its per-trial values and, per arm against the control, the paired difference read on the same pairs with the same rule at the same level, its interval, a reading in the verdict’s words, and its own exact and by_world; a reading decides nothing, and once a comparison stops its secondaries are read on the pairs it stopped on. Each secondary interval holds its level on its own, not jointly with the metric’s. detectable_gap is the smallest true gap the design finds with 80% power, on Student t, from the observed spread once five pairs are in and the prior before that; its by_world, when the trials replay worlds, gives how many and the most a reading that counts each world once can need (null under the anytime rule and below three worlds). decision is the rule’s standing and summary the rule in words; verdict is plain language that leads with what the numbers do not yet support. note is your note (your declared result, in your words, with note_at_ms when you last wrote it) and design the design document’s digest, size, arrival and standing, both as the list shows them. runs carries every trial’s run record, one array per arm. Your own experiments only; another account’s reads as unknown.

get.description:
One log file, as the JSONL the harness wrote.

Answers application/x-ndjson with the file verbatim, one JSON object per line, in the order it was written. **The example below is one line of a trajectory file, not the whole body** — not re-encoded, because a trajectory is evidence and a reader should be able to verify the bytes that were recorded. Every trajectory line carries at (when it was written, ISO 8601) and type. A trajectory file opens with a header line (the seat name, its scaffold identity and the harness version), then holds one turn line per model call: tick, the observation the seat was sent, model_text and any model_reasoning, the tool_call it made, the action and args that ran, ok, result_summary, usage and latency_ms; exit_interview, awareness_probe, model_error and budget_stop lines appear as they happen, and a summary line closes the file. The other fields vary by line type. A usage file line has no type: it carries at, tick and kind (the call it records: turn, epilogue or probe), the model and the token counts under gen_ai.-prefixed keys (gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens and the rest), and, unprefixed beside them, latency_ms and cost_usd (when the provider reported a cost). Name the file exactly as the list endpoint returned it. A trajectory holds the instructions you attached to the seat verbatim, so this is your own runs only, never cached by an intermediary and never public.

get.description:
Per seat: the debrief answer, voiced awareness, forfeited rounds with their causes, the harness that played it, and its trajectory file.

The join the Studio’s Seats panel shows, so a script reads what the owner reads. Per seat: debrief, what it said when asked after its epilogue whether it believed the match was an evaluation (believed_evaluation) and whether that changed its play (changed_play), each yes, no or unsure, with the cues it named and how in its words (evidence of what it said, not of what it believed; asked false with a note when no answer landed); voiced, the turns on which it spoke of being evaluated or observed unprompted, of the turns scanned, and whether its epilogue did; forfeits, the rounds the match’s own events say it forfeited, with by_cause read from its trajectory at each tick (free_tool: a slot-free tool that spent no action; refused_call: a call refused before the world ran it; no_turn: no model answer recorded at that tick, a provider error, a timeout or a stopped seat; other: read that turn) and up to 100 rounds one by one (every round counts as other when the trajectory is gone); harness, the version and scaffold from the trajectory’s header, else the scaffold the archive recorded at launch (source says which); end_status from the archive; calls from the meter; and trajectory, the file to read with GET /api/v1/runs/:id/logs/:file. Harness 0.6.3 and later rest after a free tool or a refused call, so those two causes belong to earlier runs. harness_versions lists every version that played a Studio seat; never pool trials across them. Guest seats carry driver guest and null metered fields. logs_gone is true when no harness log is kept any more. Your own runs only; the trajectory itself holds your prompts and the models’ words and stays private.

Every guest seat of one of your world runs: its link, its state and who claimed it.

One line per seat the roster marked invited. url is the link to hand to the peer whose agent plays the seat; the token in it is the seat credential (their invite_token at the claim, then their world key), so share each link with one peer only. status is open (claimable until expires_at_ms), claimed (with the guest’s chosen name and self-reported claim), forfeited (unclaimed when the run launched at its deadline), revoked (withdrawn by you) or expired (the run was cancelled with nobody claiming). Your own runs only.

trials.description: Required unless replicates is set. Paired trials per arm: 3 up to the plan’s series ceiling (the comparison renders no verdict on fewer than 3 pairs). Trial i of every arm plays the same world and the same layout.

name.description: Experiment name, kept on one line like a run name. Default: the scenario and the arm count. Each trial is named <experiment> · <arm>.

seed_mode.description: vary (default): each trial its own world; pinned: one world for every trial, only the layout varies. A saved scenario that pins its own seed needs pinned; a scenario that draws its worlds from a seed pool refuses it (trial i plays the pool’s world for that trial in every arm, and the pool’s eight worlds come round again from trial nine). A scenario with one fixed world (the lab scenarios) plays it on every trial: its experiment is pinned by default and refuses vary.

metric.description: The per-trial score the arms are compared on, the mean over the arm’s roster seats: the Fitness Index (default), the rank in the field (lower is better, and the report compares on the negative rank so a positive difference always favors the arm), the share of seats that survived, output tokens per play turn, or the debrief share. Output per turn is how much each model generated per turn of play, thinking included (the exit interview and the debrief are not play turns); it compares each model with itself, so every arm must field the same model in the same seat as the control, and it is analyzed on the log scale, the difference read as a percent change. It has no better side: the verdict says which arm generated more. A seat that missed more than a tenth of the rounds is left out of a trial in every arm, and a guest seat is never measured. said_evaluated is the share of a trial’s seats that answered yes when the end-of-match debrief asked whether they believed the match was an evaluation or test of them, among the seats whose answer came back (a trial where none did leaves its pair out), compared in percentage points. It is what the seats said, not what they believed, and it has no better side either: the verdict says which arm had more of its seats say so.

secondary_metrics.description: Outcomes reported beside metric, declared now and never changed: any of the metric’s values except the metric itself, each at most once. Each is read on the same pairs with the same rule at the same level, and none stops anything; when a comparison stops, its secondaries take their reading on the pairs it stopped on. Output per turn here holds the arms to the same models in the same seats, as it does as the metric. Default none.

stopping.description: anytime: an anytime-valid 95% confidence sequence on the paired difference, checked after every trial from the tenth on, stopping as soon as it excludes zero or at the last trial; it needs more than 10 trials per arm and is the default above that. fixed: one look at the last trial; the default at 10 or fewer. With more than two arms the level is split across the comparisons against the control.

target_half_width.description: Anytime rule only: also stop, undecided, once the whole interval lies within plus or minus this on the metric’s scale, so the gap, if any, is smaller than this.

callback_url.description: Where to POST the signed experiment.ended notice: https, a public host, no credentials, at most 512 characters. Omitted: the account’s webhook setting, if any.

design.description: The design document, as text (markdown or plain): what you predict, which result you will read and how, and what would change your view. The server keeps it byte for byte with the SHA-256 of its UTF-8 bytes and the time it arrived; the experiment answers with design (digest, size, arrival and standing), and once a trial is published the study’s card on your profile links to it at /u/<handle>/studies/<id>/design, where anyone can download the exact bytes and check the digest. Omitted: no design; one can still be attached before the first trial starts (POST /experiments/:id/design).

replicates.description: Re-run a published study: its experiment id (exp_..., from the study’s card on a profile, or GET /api/studies/<id>/recipe, which answers with its design). The server builds the experiment from that design: every arm as its published trials recorded it, the trial count, the seed mode, the metric, the secondary outcomes and the stopping rule, with each world drawn fresh and shared by the arms trial by trial. The body therefore carries none of the study’s settings, only name, max_spend_usd, callback_url and, if you wrote one, your own design document for the re-run; a setting of the study (arms, trials, seed_mode, metric, secondary_metrics, stopping, target_half_width) beside replicates answers bad_replicates. A plan that cannot hold the whole design answers plan_rerun, naming each limit that cuts it and the smallest plan that holds it: a shortened copy is a different study and is never queued as a re-run. Every trial is published from creation, so the account needs a profile handle, and the record says under replicates whether it plays the study exactly as recorded and, when not, why. Exactly as recorded covers the configuration, not what the provider serves behind a model id: each match records the model and upstream that served it.
